entities.summary: Eugène Henri Paul Gauguin was a French painter, sculptor, printmaker, ceramist, and writer, whose work has been primarily associated with the Post-Impressionist and Symbolist movements. He was also an influential practitioner of wood engraving and woodcuts as art forms. While only moderately successful during his lifetime, Gauguin has since been recognized for his experimental use of color and Synthetist style that were distinct from Impressionism. Paul Gauguin was a painters & sculptors from Paris (1848-06-07, Paris–1903-05-08). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gauguin's experimental use of color and Synthetist style influenced Post-Impressionism and contributed to the development of modern art. His work had a significant impact on the artistic movement, with his paintings selling for millions after his death.
